title: Chapter 11: Security Analysis, General Approach; Zweig commentary

claims.text: Detailed mathematics does not make uncertain long-range assumptions reliable. Show how much estimated value depends on forecasts rather than observed earning power.
claims.anchor: more vulnerable it becomes to possible miscalculation

claims.text: Debt analysis should combine earnings coverage with financial structure, operating resilience and realistic asset recovery; the source's numerical thresholds are conventions, not uniquely determined safety boundaries.
Avoid counting management quality repeatedly in historical profitability, forecast growth and a separate valuation premium.

The growth-multiple formula is illustrative and is not certified as a reliable valuation model. Any present-value estimate needs explicit interest-rate, duration, reinvestment and terminal assumptions.

Preserve a valuation based on observed history separately from modifications for expected changes, with reasons and timestamps for every modification. Even a transparent process needs outcome validation.
claims.anchor: both the original valuation and the modified one

claims.text: Read multiple annual reports for sources of growth, financing dependence, customer concentration, executive promises and repeated adjustments rather than relying on the latest headline earnings.

Use the owner-cash concept with a reconciled calculation rather than mechanically applying the commentary's abbreviated formula; maintenance investment, working capital, option economics and already-recognized charges must not be omitted or counted twice.

assimilation: Maintain an auditable base valuation and a separately reasoned scenario adjustment. Inputs carry source dates and uncertainty, and future revisions must not overwrite prior forecasts. Use cash generation, liabilities and governance evidence to test the story. A completed foundation permits bounded research; the chapter explicitly does not certify independent security-selection competence.
adversarial_review: Past debt coverage cannot guarantee future solvency; the source's near-impossibility of utility failure is too strong. Aggregate forecast errors can cancel and conceal large name-level errors. The stated infinite value at 8% growth depends on a discount-rate convention and indefinite growth; 8% is not a universal mathematical boundary. Table 11-5 is an illustrative selected comparison, not out-of-sample certification. Historical pretax growth does not convert to a lower after-tax growth rate merely by multiplying by a constant tax rate. Owner earnings require working-capital and maintenance-capex analysis; subtracting extraordinary charges already in net income could double count. Option overhang is contingent and exercise brings proceeds; adding all options unconditionally overstates dilution. A record-high repurchase price need not exceed intrinsic value, and price underperformance alone does not prove retained capital was misused. None of the dated thresholds becomes an execution rule.
memory_delta: Expose valuation sensitivity and avoid duplicate quality premiums. Preserve base estimates and dated scenario overrides. Reconcile reported earnings to cash and dilution without double counting; distinguish confidence in a business from confidence in the price paid.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 263-288 and inspected tables 11-1 through 11-5, including coverage exclusions, split adjustments and forecast/actual date labels.
